text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi is completing his China visit with two days in the neighbouring province of Yunnan in an effort to boost cross-border trade.
-- National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh wants the police force to make greater efforts to stop crime.

-- Ho Chi Minh City-based banks have guaranteed $3.3 billion of foreign trade settlements in the past six months, equivalent to the same period of last year. Vietcombank accounted for 34 percent of that sum.

-- The newly elected National Assembly will meet on September 20, when leaders of the state will be elected. These include the state president, the legislature's chairman, the heads of assembly committees and the prime minister. It will also ratify the list of deputy prime ministers and nominated by the new prime minister.
-- 188,000 tonnes of rice were exported through Saigon Port in the first 13 days of July, taking the amount sold abroad so far this year to more than 2.02 million tonnes.

-- The National Assembly's Standing Board has called on all the people and soldiers to take participate actively in the coming election to the legislature and for social order and security to be maintained during the voting period.
-- Hanoi's banks took $1.4 billion in new credit during the first half of 1997.
-- Ho Chi Minh City is reinforcing measures to maintain social order and security ahead of the National Assembly election.
